radial_variance_proof: R=norm(X) belongs to Gaussian W^{1,2}, with weak-gradient norm one almost everywhere. R(-X)=R(X), so its centered Hermite expansion has only even degrees at least two. Gaussian derivative Parseval gives sum k||P_k R||_2^2=1. Thus VarR<=1/2, and (ER)^2/d=(d-VarR)/d>=1-1/(2d).
rational_loss_comparison: The cutoff probability p<=d^-4 gives sqrt(p)<=d^-2. Since sqrt(1+2/(d+2))<=1+1/(d+2) and the bulk/tail coefficients are nonnegative for 0<b<1, the displayed rational Lbar dominates the exact midpoint error. Subtracting total entry approximation d^-2 and using scalar denominator B+d^-2 preserves the lower ratio bound.
rate_scope: The certified lower bounds tend to1/B at O(d^-1), or O(n^-4) after d=n^4. No quantitative denominator convergence rate or equality N=B is asserted.
independent_review: Analytic derivation, not a replay of a producer numerical claim.
